question_stem:
Four diodes are used in a bridge rectifier circuit to produce rectification of a sinusoidal a.c. input voltage $V_{IN}$.
Fig. 7.1 shows part of the circuit, but three of the diodes are missing.
{{figure:figure_7_1}}
Fig. 7.1
The p.d. across the load resistor R is the output p.d. $V_{OUT}$ of the bridge rectifier.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the name of the type of rectification produced by a bridge rectifier.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Complete Fig. 7.1 by drawing the three missing diodes, correctly connected.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 7.1, draw an arrow to indicate the direction of the current in resistor $R$.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
(b)(ii)
parts.text:
The power dissipated in the resistor is $P$.
On Fig. 7.4, sketch the variation of $P$ with $t$ between $t = 0$ and $t = 2.0T$.
{{figure:figure_7_4}}
Fig. 7.4

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest, with a reason, how the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) value of $V_{OUT}$ compares with the r.m.s. value of $V_{IN}$.
